name: Board orientation
description: Recognizing the board's layout and which side is which.

name: Square identification
description: Reading a square's file and rank without needing to memorize notation.

name: Rook movement
description: The rook moves in straight lines, any distance, until blocked.

name: Bishop movement
description: The bishop moves diagonally, any distance, until blocked, and stays on one square colour for the whole game.

name: Queen movement
description: The queen combines rook and bishop movement.

name: King movement
description: The king moves one square in any direction.

name: Knight movement
description: The knight moves in an L-shape and is the only piece that can jump over others.

name: Pawn movement
description: Pawns move forward but capture diagonally, with a two-square option on their first move.

name: Captures
description: Removing an opponent's piece by moving onto its square, following the capturing piece's own movement rules.

name: Blocked paths
description: A sliding piece (rook, bishop, queen) stops at the first piece in its path; it can capture an enemy piece there but never jumps over anything.

name: Piece values
description: The rough relative value of each piece, used to judge whether a trade is favourable.

name: King safety and castling
description: Recognizing that a king left in the centre is exposed, and using castling to bring it to safety while activating a rook.

name: Check
description: Recognizing when a king is under direct attack and must escape immediately.

name: Checkmate
description: Check with no way out — the game ends immediately.

name: Decision-making under check
description: A reliable order (capture, block, move) for finding the best response to check.

name: Back-rank safety
description: Recognizing when a castled king has no escape from a check along its own back rank, and creating luft before it's forced.

name: Tactics
description: Forcing sequences that win material or deliver checkmate.

name: Forks
description: One piece attacking two enemy targets at once.

name: Knight forks
description: A fork delivered by a knight, exploiting its L-shaped jump to attack two unrelated squares from one spot.

name: Hanging pieces
description: A piece that's attacked and has no defender — free material for whoever notices first.

name: Opening development: minor pieces before the queen
description: Bringing knights and bishops out before the queen, so an early queen move isn't just chased around and loses tempo.

name: Trade evaluation
description: Counting what a capture actually wins, and what the opponent wins back, before playing it — recognizing a losing trade even when the move itself is legal.

name: Opposition and key squares
description: In a king-and-pawn ending, a mistake can throw away a position that was winning or drawing — recognizing that these endings need their own careful technique, not just piece-counting.

name: The knight
description: General knight-piece familiarity — distinct from knight-movement (meet-the-pieces' piece-rules lesson) and knight-fork (the tactic); tags content that's simply about the knight as a piece.

name: Step-type preview
description: Tags the non-curated demo lesson exercising newly-added exercise-step types — not real curriculum content, see packages/content/units/step-type-preview.
